summary: Feed s170_triple is degraded: 3 faults detected. VLAN 20 is completely missing (50% untagged), NDR 10G port is severely oversubscribed with 24.73 Gbps bursts (247% capacity), and 94.7% encrypted traffic exceeds NDR 90% tolerance. NDR requires both directions and full payload with VLANs 10,20.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker egress is stripping 802.1Q tags or ingress trunk not configured to forward VLAN 20. 50% of packets arrive untagged and VLAN 20 is never observed, while NDR requires VLANs 10 and 20. Classic broker VLAN passthrough misconfiguration.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR loses segmentation context for VLAN 20, cannot attribute detections to correct tenant/segment, misses lateral movement and VLAN-hopping attacks; 50% of traffic lacks classification.

recommended_fix.why: Restore end-to-end 802.1Q preservation so NDR receives both required VLANs for correct policy and detection correlation.

findings.root_cause: Single 10 Gbps NDR port fed by aggregated/bursty traffic peaking at 24.73 Gbps in 1ms burst (247% of capacity). No load balancing or burst buffering on packet broker, so egress oversubscribes tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR drops packets during bursts, breaks TCP reassembly and flow reconstruction, causes missed detections and false negatives exactly when traffic spikes (often during attacks).

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across 3x10G NDR cluster members with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port load <80% and prevent drops while preserving flow stickiness.

findings.root_cause: 94.7% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) vs NDR tolerance of 90%. Traffic is predominantly encrypted without selective decryption or enriched metadata, and NDR needs full payload.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot inspect payload for signatures, exploits, or C2; detection degrades to metadata-only (JA3, SNI, flow stats), reducing coverage for encrypted attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt selectively or enrich with TLS metadata before NDR so it regains payload visibility without exceeding privacy/compliance limits.
